Teraz w warsztacie są dwie nowe lampy. Tu jest biała lampa; tam jest czerwona lampa. Dwie lampy są na podłodze. Stara lampa jest na starym stole. Jan pokazuje stary rysunek: lampa, strzałka i koło. Ale Ala pokazuje dwie nowe lampy, nie papier.

Ala bierze białą lampę i kładzie lampę tu. Ewa pokazuje kabel. Biała lampa ma kabel. Czerwona lampa ma kabel. Tu są dwa kable. Jan widzi dwa kable. Czerwony stół jest zły. Biała lampa stoi na podłodze.
Jan pokazuje stary rysunek. Ala mówi: „Na papierze jest lampa, strzałka i koło. Tu są nowe lampy.” Pokazuje białą lampę, nie papier.

Tu jest biała lampa. Tu jest światło. To jest sprawna lampa. Ala pokazuje światło, potem kabel. Biała lampa ma sprawny kabel. Ewa pokazuje czerwoną lampę. Tu nie ma światła. Kabel ma pęknięcie. To jest zepsuty kabel. Czerwona lampa jest zepsuta. Ewa nie bierze kabla.

grammar.title: Gramatyka
grammar.rule: Tu są dwie nowe lampy. Ala pokazuje dwie nowe lampy. Jan widzi cztery książki i trzy krzesła.
grammar.note_en:
Plural means more than one. This chapter teaches the nominative and accusative plural of nouns that do not refer to male people. The nominative names what is present: W warsztacie są dwie nowe lampy means “There are two new lamps in the workshop”. The accusative names the affirmative direct object: Ala pokazuje dwie nowe lampy means “Ala shows two new lamps”. Here the noun and adjective look the same in both cases; their job changes with the sentence. Do not treat an unchanged spelling as proof that there is no case.

Compare the naming forms lampa → lampy (“lamp → lamps”), kabel → kable (“cable → cables”), narzędzie → narzędzia (“tool → tools”), krzesło → krzesła (“chair → chairs”), książka → książki (“book → books”), część → części (“part → parts”), and torba → torby (“bag → bags”). Learn these actual complete forms. Kabel loses its internal e in kable; a single ending is not enough to reconstruct every noun. Część is feminine although it does not end in -a. Its plural części is shown as a present group and as an affirmative object. The lesson does not provide its whole case paradigm. Lampy and narzędzia already had a different grammatical job in earlier singular genitive examples; the count and governing construction identify their plural use here.

Dwa and dwie both mean “two”. Use dwie with the feminine nouns demonstrated here: dwie lampy, dwie torby, dwie części, dwie książki (“two lamps, bags, parts, books”). Kable is masculine inanimate and narzędzia is neuter: dwa kable, dwa narzędzia and dwa krzesła mean “two cables, two tools, two chairs”. Masculine inanimate and neuter take dwa in these examples; feminine takes dwie. Trzy means “three” and cztery “four”: trzy krzesła / cztery książki means “three chairs / four books”. The same forms occur in Jan widzi cztery książki i trzy krzesła, “Jan sees four books and three chairs”. These numerals do not take a special object spelling here. Higher numbers and plural oblique cases come later.

The nonpersonal plural adjectives shown are nowe (“new”), sprawne (“working/functioning”) and zepsute (“broken/faulty”). Dwie nowe lampy means “two new lamps”; sprawne krzesła means “working chairs”; zepsute części means “broken parts”. Their ending -e is used in the demonstrated naming and affirmative object phrases. This is not a table for human male groups or for every plural case. Singular forms remain useful: sprawna lampa / sprawny kabel means “a functioning lamp / cable”; zepsuta lampa / zepsuty kabel means “a broken lamp / cable”. Sprawną lampę and zepsutą lampę are the feminine singular object phrases after widzi. The familiar singular -a → -ą adjective change accompanies lampa → lampę.

Only być has plural verb forms here. Lampy są na podłodze means “The lamps are on the floor”; Jan widzi lampy means “Jan sees the lamps”. Jan is one actor, so widzi stays singular although his object is plural. Ewa bierze narzędzia / Ala przesuwa krzesła means “Ewa takes tools / Ala moves chairs”: the object count does not turn one actor into several. Other plural action verbs and human-role plurals are next chapter. Negated plural objects, plural possessives, directional phrases and source phrases are not taught here. The familiar singular possession statements remain singular: moje narzędzie (“my tool”), nasz młotek (“our hammer”) and nasza pomoc (“our help”). Nasza agrees with singular feminine pomoc; it is not a plural adjective.

Sprawny describes function. The new white lamp supplies light; the new red cable has a visible break and remains disconnected. Observed function does not certify electrical safety, and an intact-looking cable alone would not prove safety. The original lamp and its cracked cable are distinct and remain untouched and untested. Część means a part of a whole: the diagram relates a lamp to its cable without teaching a noun-dependent genitive. The box’s existing screw is kept separate from the loose broken new cable and distinct damaged screw.

The new SMS says My jesteśmy w Łodzi. Czy jest potrzebna nasza pomoc?—“We are in Łódź. Is our help needed?” Its written my refers to the senders, not to the people reading the phone. Their offer does not establish an arrival at the workshop. The earlier Jestem właścicielem (“I am the owner”) is a different message from the absent owner. The two street labels remain separate information; neither a lamp owner nor the source of the unclaimed small tool is identified.
